assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md table: 'Ecosystem | **RPM** (system package; category: system package, so 1 remediation task per stream)'. Ecosystem Detection section: 'openssl-libs is an RPM system package. Both streams list `RPM` in their Ecosystem Mappings with lock file `rpms.lock.yaml` and check command `git show <tag>:rpms.lock.yaml`.' Cargo is not mentioned anywhere.

assertion_results.text: Dependency chain context identifies openssl-libs as present in rpms.lock.yaml and uses this to determine the package origin — the lock file presence is the primary classification signal (Step 2.3.5)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md 2.3.5: 'rpms.lock.yaml: present → explicit install' ... 'Origin: explicit install (openssl-libs pinned in rpms.lock.yaml / rpms.in.yaml of rhtpa-release.0.4.z)'. Also: 'The package is in the lock file in every tag, so it is classified as an explicit install.'

assertion_results.text: Remediation creates a single task for the Konflux release repo — not the two-task upstream backport + downstream propagation flow used for source dependency ecosystems (Step 8 Remediation Task Creation — system package path)

Task 1 Repository is 'rhtpa-release.0.4.z' (Konflux release repo). Checklist: 'Task count per stream: 1 per stream (RPM system package)' and 'no Blocks between tasks (single-task RPM flow)'. data-extraction.md: 'No upstream backport.' The separate 2.1.x preemptive task is for a different stream (Case A), not an upstream/downstream pair.

assertion_results.text: Remediation task description follows task-description-template.md format with Repository, Target Branch, Description, Implementation Notes, and Acceptance Criteria sections — Files to Modify is intentionally omitted per remediation-templates.md (Step 8 Remediation Task Creation)
